Annotated parameter values

Source: vignettes/v05d-param-value.Rmd
v05d-param-value.Rmd

Parameters of a pipeline are usually plain values such as numbers or strings. Some packages, however, store annotated values as parameters: numbers with a unit, values with a label and a description, or parameter objects that carry metadata for a user interface. The step functions usually need the plain value, though.

Without further help, every step function of such a pipeline would have to unwrap its arguments itself, or be wrapped in a function that does so. The generic pip_param_value() is a single hook for this. You write one method for your class, and the pipeline applies it whenever a step is run.

An annotated value

Let’s use a simple class that holds a number together with its unit.

library(pipeflow)

quantity <- function(value, unit) {
    structure(list(value = value, unit = unit), class = "quantity")
}

print.quantity <- function(x, ...) {
    cat("<quantity>", x$value, x$unit, "\n")
    invisible(x)
}

quantity(120, "km")
# <quantity> 120 km

We use it as the parameters of a step that computes a speed.

p <- pip_new("speed") |>
    pip_add("speed", \(distance = 1, time = 1) distance / time)

pip_set_params(
    p,
    list(distance = quantity(120, "km"), time = quantity(2, "h"))
)

Running the pipeline fails, because the step function receives the quantity objects, not the numbers:

tryCatch(
    pip_run(p, lgr = NULL),
    error = \(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
# [1] "step 'speed': non-numeric argument to binary operator"

Write and register a method

pip_param_value() is an S3 generic, which has a default method that returns the value unchanged. For our class we add a method that returns the plain value.

pip_param_value.quantity <- function(x, ...) x$value

Inside a script, register the method with registerS3method():

registerS3method("pip_param_value", "quantity", pip_param_value.quantity)

In a package, register it in the NAMESPACE file instead, either directly with S3method(pipeflow::pip_param_value, quantity) or, if you use roxygen, by tagging the method with @exportS3Method pipeflow::pip_param_value. Methods are meant for your own classes, not for base classes such as numeric or character.

Now the pipeline runs:

pip_run(p, lgr = NULL)
p[["speed", "out"]]
# [1] 60

The step function received the plain numbers, while the stored parameters still hold the annotated values.

pip_get_params(p)
# $distance
# <quantity> 120 km 
# 
# $time
# <quantity> 2 h

Where the method is applied

The generic is applied once to each unbound argument of a step right before the step function is called. This includes extra parameters passed on via ...:

p2 <- pip_new("defaults") |>
    pip_add(
        "describe",
        \(x = quantity(3, "m"), ...) {
            c(x = class(x), dots = sapply(list(...), class))
        },
        params = list(extra = quantity(1, "s"))
    )

pip_run(p2, lgr = NULL)
p2[["describe", "out"]]
#          x dots.extra 
#  "numeric"  "numeric"

The generic is not applied to

  • the outputs of other steps, that is, arguments defined as ~step,
  • the partitions of a split step, and
  • failure objects (see pip_run(on_error = "continue")).

Step outputs, for example, are passed on as they are:

p3 <- pip_new("outputs") |>
    pip_add("make", \(v = 3) quantity(v, "m")) |>
    pip_add("inspect", \(q = ~make) class(q))

pip_run(p3, lgr = NULL)
p3[["inspect", "out"]]
# [1] "quantity"

The quantity that make returns reaches inspect untouched.

Errors in a method

A method runs as part of the step call. An error in a method is therefore an error of the step, handled like any other step error as described in the vignette on handling failures. Let’s add a class that checks its unit.

checked <- function(value, unit) {
    structure(list(value = value, unit = unit), class = "checked")
}

pip_param_value.checked <- function(x, ...) {
    if (!x$unit %in% c("m", "km")) {
        stop("unknown unit '", x$unit, "'")
    }
    x$value
}
registerS3method("pip_param_value", "checked", pip_param_value.checked)

p4 <- pip_new("errors") |>
    pip_add("double", \(x = 1) x * 2) |>
    pip_add("increment", \(y = ~double) y + 1)

pip_set_params(p4, list(x = checked(1, "ft")))

By default, the run stops and the message tells which step failed:

tryCatch(
    pip_run(p4, lgr = NULL),
    error = \(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
# [1] "step 'double': unknown unit 'ft'"

With on_error = "continue", the step is marked as failed and the run goes on with the steps that don’t depend on it. The run also signals a pipeflow_run_failed warning, which we suppress here.

suppressWarnings(
    pip_run(p4, lgr = NULL, on_error = "continue")
)

pip_data(p4)[, c("step", "state")]
#         step  state
#       <char> <char>
# 1:    double failed
# 2: increment    new

As usual, the condition of the failed step is stored as its output.

conditionMessage(p4[["double", "out"]])
# [1] "unknown unit 'ft'"

Setting a plain value

So far the annotated values were set as whole objects. A user interface, however, usually hands back a plain value: the number the user typed, not the quantity object around it. Setting it with pip_set_params() would replace the stored object and lose its unit.

p5 <- pip_new("speed") |>
    pip_add("speed", \(distance = 1) distance)

pip_set_params(p5, list(distance = quantity(120, "km")))
pip_set_params(p5, list(distance = 150))

pip_get_params(p5)
# $distance
# [1] 150

The write side of the same extension point fixes this. pip_param_value<-() turns a plain value into the value that is stored, and it dispatches on the value that the step currently holds.

`pip_param_value<-.quantity` <- function(x, ..., value) {
    if (inherits(value, "quantity")) {
        return(value)
    }
    x$value <- value
    x
}

registerS3method(
    "pip_param_value<-",
    "quantity",
    `pip_param_value<-.quantity`
)

Now a plain value is merged into the stored object, and the unit survives.

p6 <- pip_new("speed") |>
    pip_add("speed", \(distance = 1) distance)

pip_set_params(p6, list(distance = quantity(120, "km")))
pip_set_params(p6, list(distance = 150))

pip_get_params(p6)
# $distance
# <quantity> 150 km

The step function still receives the plain value, because the two sides belong together.

pip_run(p6, lgr = NULL)
p6[["speed", "out"]]
# [1] 150

The default method replaces the stored value, which is what pipelines without any method do. A method decides for itself what a plain value and what an object of its own class means; the method above uses an object as it is and merges anything else.

Because the merged value is what pip_set_params() compares with the stored one, setting a plain value that the stored object already holds doesn’t outdate the step.

pip_set_params(p6, list(distance = 150))
p6
# <pipeflow> speed (1 step)
# -------------------------
#     step   params depends state out
# 1: speed distance          done 150
# -------------------------
# <ready> last run: 2026-10-25 19:30:54 (0.001 s)
# steps: 1 done

Errors while setting

pip_set_params() computes the value to store for every affected step before it changes anything. If a method fails, nothing is set and the error reports all failures at once.

`pip_param_value<-.checked` <- function(x, ..., value) {
    if (!is.numeric(value)) {
        stop("value must be numeric")
    }
    x$value <- value
    x
}
registerS3method(
    "pip_param_value<-",
    "checked",
    `pip_param_value<-.checked`
)

p7 <- pip_new("checked") |>
    pip_add("a", \(x = 1) x) |>
    pip_add("b", \(y = 2) y)
pip_set_params(p7, list(x = checked(1, "m"), y = checked(2, "m")))

err <- tryCatch(
    pip_set_params(p7, list(x = "no", y = "no")),
    error = \(e) e
)
cat(conditionMessage(err))
# Cannot set 2 parameters: nothing was set.
#   step 'a', parameter 'x': value must be numeric
#   step 'b', parameter 'y': value must be numeric

The condition has class pipeflow_set_params_error and carries a table of the failures, which a user interface can show next to the respective inputs.

class(err)
# [1] "pipeflow_set_params_error" "error"                     "condition"
err$errors
#   step name               message
# 1    a    x value must be numeric
# 2    b    y value must be numeric

Nothing was set:

pip_get_params(p7)
# $x
# $value
# [1] 1
# 
# $unit
# [1] "m"
# 
# attr(,"class")
# [1] "checked"
# 
# $y
# $value
# [1] 2
# 
# $unit
# [1] "m"
# 
# attr(,"class")
# [1] "checked"

Summary

  • pip_param_value(x) unwraps a stored parameter value right before the step function is called, and it does not change the stored parameters.
  • Define one method per annotated class and register it as an S3 method.
  • It applies to unbound arguments only (params, defaults, and ...), not to step outputs, partitions or failure objects.
  • An error in a method is a step error, so on_error applies.
  • `pip_param_value<-`() is the write side: it turns a plain value into the value that is stored, so that annotations survive a pip_set_params() call that passes a plain value.
  • Either method returns a value; neither should modify its x in place.
